children: Peru's central bank held its benchmark interest rate at 4.25% on Thursday, extending its pause for a 12th straight meeting, in line with market expectations.
Annual inflation in one of the world's largest copper producers accelerated to 4.44% in the 12 months through August, remaining above the central bank's 1% to 3% target range.
"The inflation rate's deviation from the target range was driven mainly by higher fuel prices and their impact on transportation costs in March and April," the central bank said in a statement.

The bank cautioned that weather-related disruptions from El Niño and geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East could prolong inflation, though it still expects the rate to ease back to its 2% target.

The central bank has kept borrowing costs steady since September 2025, after a series of earlier rate cuts, as policymakers assess persistent price pressures linked largely to supply shocks such as higher fuel costs.
